Format metadata for analysis.

prepare_metadata.Rd

From a sf object containing patch and individual IDs as well as environmental variables, create the three metadata input files required by mechGEA. An example input is in sample_metadata. An example output is in example_gl.

Usage

prepare_metadata(sample_meta, env_mean_method = "unweighted", idp = 1)

Arguments

sample_meta

sf POINT geometry containing two required columns: patch containing patch IDs and ind_id containing individual IDs. Additional columns specify named environmental variables. Patches must be in continuous blocks and sorted identically to the likelihood data also provided to mechGEA. NOTE: .beagle or .beagle.gz files can be re-sorted on import using the beagle2pl function.

env_mean_method

character, default "unweighted". Specifies how environmental variables are averaged across samples. Options:

  • "unweighted": direct means across samples within patches.

  • "weighted": inverse-distance scaled averages. Scaling power given by idp.

idp

integer, default 1. Inverse-distance power used for weighted environmental averages. Ignored if env_mean_method == "weighted". Higher values give less weight to points distant from the patch centroid.
